Lavender EO (French, L. angustifolia).source: GC-MS of commercial market samples: linalyl acetate 37.8, linalool 33.1, eucalyptol 4.9, camphor 4.1; terpinen-4-ol ~2 and lavandulyl acetate ~2 from the same literature range.
Lavender EO (French, L. angustifolia).note: The default for an unqualified 'lavender oil' in a perfumery formula. Terpinen-4-ol and lavandulyl acetate were previously omitted for want of library entries.

Lavender EO (Spanish, var. pyrenaica).source: linalool 38.0, borneol 19.7, camphor 8.1, cineole ~3, linalyl acetate ~1.1

Lavender EO (South African).note: Barely a lavender by odour; kept as the negative control, since a method that calls this one lavender is not discriminating.

Petitgrain EO (bigarade).source: Supplier GC-MS of one batch with 27 components quantified: linalyl acetate 51.1, linalool 23.6, alpha-terpineol 5.3, geranyl acetate 3.8, neryl acetate 2.2. Across eight batches from the same source linalyl acetate runs 37-51 and linalool 20-29. Geraniol 2.5 is the midpoint of a vendor range of 2-3. The terpene hydrocarbons and nerolidol are typical leaf-oil figures rather than this batch's, and are the weakest numbers here.
Petitgrain EO (bigarade).note: Replaces an entry built from range midpoints with six constituents. The perfumer judged a two-material metamer of that version really close, but found petitgrain carrying extra spice in the background. A six-constituent build could not contain that and this one may still not: no source gives a spicy constituent for petitgrain bigarade, so if the spice is real it sits in a trace for which nobody has published a figure.

Cedarwood EO (Virginia).source: Virginia cedarwood: alpha-cedrene ~24, thujopsene ~21, cedrol ~19, beta-cedrene ~8, alpha-cuparene ~4, widdrol ~3.5. The first three are the usual commercial specification.
Cedarwood EO (Virginia).note: Thujopsene is a fifth of this oil and was omitted because the library had no entry for it. With thujopsene, beta-cedrene, cuparene and widdrol the build covers about 80% of the oil instead of 43%. Cedarwood EO was also the single most extreme point on the published atlas under noisy-OR, so its position should be worth re-reading after this.

Bergamot EO (Turkish).source: Peer-reviewed analysis of Turkish bergamot oil, 2000: linalyl acetate 38.7, limonene 23.7, linalool 14.7, gamma-terpinene 4.7, beta-pinene 3.0, myrcene 2.0.
Bergamot EO (Turkish).note: Other origins range linalyl acetate 19-41%, limonene 24-44%, linalool 7-26%, so this is one profile out of a wide family.

Geranium EO (Bourbon, Madagascar).source: Bourbon geranium: citronellol ~30, geraniol ~16, isomenthone 8.2, citronellyl formate ~7.
Geranium EO (Bourbon, Madagascar).note: Isomenthone carries much of this oil's minty-green edge and was omitted for want of a library entry.

Peppermint EO (Michigan).source: Michigan peppermint: menthol ~38, menthone ~20, cineole ~6, menthyl acetate 3.7, menthofuran 2.5.
Peppermint EO (Michigan).note: Menthyl acetate and menthofuran were both omitted for want of library entries, and menthofuran carries character well out of proportion to its 2.5%.

Lemongrass EO.source: 2025 study of Nepalese oil: neral 35.5, geranial 36.0, which together are citral. Commercial entries put citral totals at 45-70% and myrcene at 1-11%; midpoints used for the minors.
Lemongrass EO.note: In the perfumer's candidate list. Citral-dominated, and the library's Citral is itself the geranial/neral mixture, so the two isomers are entered as one material rather than double-counted. It passes its own name but sits at cosine 0.988 from plain Citral, so read it as citral with company.

Lavandin EO (Grosso).source: Lavandin Grosso: linalool ~30, linalyl acetate ~28, camphor ~7, cineole ~6, terpinen-4-ol 4.8 in one Grosso sample.
Lavandin EO (Grosso).note: A lavandin is a lavender hybrid, sold and used as a lavender, so the lavender descriptor is a fair claim to hold it to.

Clary Sage EO.source: Clary sage: linalyl acetate ~60, linalool ~18, geranyl acetate ~5, germacrene D ~4, sclareol ~1.
Clary Sage EO.note: Germacrene D and sclareol are now in the library. Sclareol is a barely volatile diterpene diol, so its contribution to a sniffed oil is smaller than 1% suggests and the model has no way to know that.

Rosemary EO (cineole type).source: Cineole-type rosemary: 1,8-cineole ~45, camphor ~12, alpha-pinene ~12, borneol ~4, camphene ~4, verbenone ~3 and up to ~8 in other chemotypes.
Rosemary EO (cineole type).note: Camphene and verbenone are now in the library. Verbenone is the marker separating rosemary chemotypes, and the low end of its range is used.

Juniper Berry EO.source: Juniper berry: alpha-pinene ~40, myrcene ~10, sabinene ~8, limonene ~5, with terpinen-4-ol and caryophyllene minor.
Juniper Berry EO.note: Sabinene and terpinen-4-ol are now in the library, so this is no longer alpha-pinene with decoration.

Thyme EO (thymol type).source: Thymol-type thyme: thymol 42, p-cymene 18.6, gamma-terpinene 9, carvacrol 4, linalool 4.
Thyme EO (thymol type).note: p-Cymene is 18.6% of this oil and was omitted for want of a library entry; it is now the second-largest constituent of the build.

Clove Bud EO (steam distilled).source: Steam-distilled clove bud: eugenol ~80, eugenyl acetate ~8, beta-caryophyllene ~7.
Clove Bud EO (steam distilled).note: Eugenyl acetate was omitted for want of a library entry; the build now covers about 95% of the oil.

Orange EO (sweet, Florida).source: Florida sweet orange: limonene ~91, myrcene ~2, with octanal and decanal at a few tenths each.
Orange EO (sweet, Florida).note: Octanal and decanal carry much of a fresh orange's top note and were recorded as omitted. They were in the library all along, as Aldehyde C-8 and Aldehyde C-10, which the earlier entry failed to notice.

Lime EO (Persian, expressed).source: Persian expressed lime: limonene ~48, beta-pinene ~14, gamma-terpinene ~12, citral ~5, with sabinene, p-cymene and terpinen-4-ol minor.
Lime EO (Persian, expressed).note: Sabinene, p-cymene and terpinen-4-ol were all recorded as omitted and are now in the library.

Tangerine EO.source: Tangerine: limonene ~95, with methyl N-methylanthranilate and thymol as the traces that distinguish it from sweet orange.
Tangerine EO.note: The earlier entry said that substituting methyl anthranilate for methyl N-methylanthranilate would be a fabrication, and left the distinction out. The real molecule is now in the library, so the distinction can be built instead of described.

Cinnamon Bark EO (commercial).source: GC-MS of commercial oil: cinnamal 63.59, eugenol 8.32, cinnamyl acetate 7.48, caryophyllene 6.88, linalool 6.31, eucalyptol 2.57.

Lemon EO (Sicilian, cold-pressed).source: GC-MS of a Sicilian cold-pressed peel oil: limonene 63.34, beta-pinene 13.55, gamma-terpinene 9.95, citral 1.88; sabinene ~2 and p-cymene ~0.5 from the same literature range.
Lemon EO (Sicilian, cold-pressed).note: Peel oil, not leaf oil: the leaf is a citral oil and a different material.

Grapefruit EO (cold-pressed).source: Cold-pressed peel oils across three varieties: d-limonene 87-90, beta-myrcene 2-4; nootkatone 0.1 and the aldehydes at a few tenths from commercial batch data.
Grapefruit EO (cold-pressed).note: Nootkatone is the grapefruit note and is a tenth of a percent of the oil, so a mass-weighted build cannot see it. This oil stays a test of exactly that failure.

Mandarin EO (Italian, cold-pressed).source: Italian peel oil (Shiota and Ito 1991): limonene 74.52, gamma-terpinene 15.5. Methyl N-methylanthranilate at 0.5 sits inside the 0.3-1.0 range the ISO 3528 batch data reports.
Mandarin EO (Italian, cold-pressed).note: Methyl N-methylanthranilate is what makes a mandarin a mandarin rather than an orange, and it is now in the library, so this is no longer limonene with decoration.

Neroli EO (Egyptian).source: Commercial Egyptian GC-MS batch (lot 13198 and a 2023 batch report): linalool 44.95-44.99, linalyl acetate 6.18-16.27, d-limonene 8.40-11.53, beta-pinene 4.93-5.93, nerolidol 2.21; peer-reviewed Egyptian survey puts linalool at 44-53% and linalyl acetate at 2-15%, so the midpoint of the acetate range is used.
Neroli EO (Egyptian).note: The formula's ingredient is a neroli *accord*, not the oil, so this stands in for it on the assumption that the accord is built towards the oil. The indole and methyl anthranilate traces are what make it read as a flower rather than as linalool with company.

Rosewood EO (Aniba rosaeodora).source: Amazonian wood oil: linalool 93.60 in one analysis and 89.34 in another of the same species; alpha-terpineol 3.54 from a commercial reference profile (2-5% across sources).
Rosewood EO (Aniba rosaeodora).note: A linalool oil with a few percent of everything else, so it should land on Linalool. Ho wood is the commercial substitute and is the same shape.

Litsea Cubeba EO (Chinese, fruit).source: Eight Chinese production regions (Cui et al., Molecules 2012): neral plus geranial 78.7-87.4 of the oil, d-limonene 0.7-5.3 in fruit oils; a Taiwanese fruit oil instead gives geranial 37.16, neral 28.29, d-limonene 22.90.
Litsea Cubeba EO (Chinese, fruit).note: The library has one Citral entry rather than separate neral and geranial, so the two are summed into it. The Chinese profile is used; the Taiwanese one is a different oil in practice, four times the limonene.

Patchouli EO (Javanese).source: Javanese oil (Lawrence 1990): patchouli alcohol 29.7, alpha-bulnesene 16.7, alpha-guaiene 13.5, seychellene 8.8, norpatchoulenol 0.8; beta-patchoulene 4.56 and trans-caryophyllene 7.96 from an Indonesian GC-MS of leaf oil; pogostol ~2 as a typical figure.
Patchouli EO (Javanese).note: Buildable only because its principal sesquiterpenoids were added as reference molecules. Norpatchoulenol is held to be the key odorant and is under 1% of the oil, so a mass-weighted build cannot see it.

Vetiver EO (Haiti).source: Champagnat et al. 2006, nine commercial origins: khusimol 3.4-13.7, vetiselinenol 1.3-7.8, alpha-vetivone 2.5-6.3, beta-vetispirene 1.6-4.5, and no meaningful difference between origins. One organic Haitian batch certificate gives khusimol 15.06, trans-isovalencenol 13.04, alpha-vetivone 4.04, khusimone 2.57; the certificate's figures are used where the study gives only a range.
Vetiver EO (Haiti).note: Vetiver has no majority constituent: it is roughly 150 sesquiterpenoids, and the named ones here total under half the oil. So this is a build from the identified fraction, renormalised, and it is the weakest build in this file for that reason. Four of its seven constituents are absent from the percept model's training set, which makes their descriptor vectors extrapolations; khusimone is in it, labelled vetiver and woody. beta-vetispirene is omitted because PubChem returned the same structure for it and for beta-vetivenene, and a wrong structure is worse than a missing one.

Ylang Ylang EO (extra).source: Range midpoints for the Extra fraction from two independent compilations that agree: benzyl acetate 15-30, linalool 7-24, p-cresyl methyl ether 7-13 (5-16 in the second), methyl benzoate 4-9, geranyl acetate 2-14. Germacrene D 4.6-8.7 and benzyl benzoate 1.6 from single-batch GC-MS certificates of Madagascan Extra lots.
Ylang Ylang EO (extra).note: Left out of this file until now because the library had no p-cresyl methyl ether, which is the molecule that makes ylang smell of ylang, and a build without it would have passed inspection while misrepresenting the oil. Extra is the first fraction and the one perfumery usually means; later fractions carry more sesquiterpene and less ester, so a formula saying only 'ylang' is underspecified. These are range midpoints, not one analysis, and the batch certificates disagree with each other on linalool by a factor of two.

Elemi EO (Manila).source: Quantitative Manila elemi: limonene 56.0, alpha-phellandrene 17.6, elemol 6.3, sabinene 5.7, beta-phellandrene 3.3, terpinolene 2.8, elemicin 2.4. Villanueva et al. 1993 identified 39 compounds making up 99.2% of the oil with limonene most abundant at 56%, which agrees. A 1984 analysis instead gives limonene 26.9, elemol 17.3 and elemicin 10.6, so batch variation here is large.
Elemi EO (Manila).note: Buildable because elemol, elemicin and alpha-phellandrene were added for it. Beta-phellandrene is still missing and is the only constituent above 3% that is.
